content.title: Why Do We Need Decision Making in Software?
content.definition: Standard programs run line-by-line in a rigid sequence. Decision-making statements evaluate live data and dynamically direct execution down different paths.
content.keyPoint: Golden Rule: Decision = (Input Data) ➔ [Condition Evaluation: True/False] ➔ (Action Execution)

content.title: Boolean Expressions & Comparison Operators
content.definition: A condition is a Boolean Expression that evaluates strictly to either True or False.

table.desc: Evaluates True if operands on both sides are identical
Evaluates True if operands on both sides are different
Greater than / Greater than or equal to
Less than / Less than or equal to

content.note: ⚠️ CRITICAL TRAP: '=' is for Assignment (x = 5), while '==' is for Equality Comparison (x == 5)!

content.title: One-Way Branch: The "if" Statement with Flowchart
content.definition: The code block inside an 'if' executes ONLY when its condition evaluates to True. If False, the block is completely bypassed.
points: Mandatory Colon (:): Must follow the condition expression.
Indentation (4 spaces): Defines the scope of the code block.
Sequential Flow: Code after the block executes unconditionally.

codeSnippet.code:
# Smart Clinic Patient Screening
temperature = 38.8

if temperature > 37.5:
    print('⚠️ Alert: High fever detected!')
    print('Please proceed to Triage Room 2.')

print('Screening check complete.')
codeSnippet.output:
⚠️ Alert: High fever detected!
Please proceed to Triage Room 2.
Screening check complete.

content.title: Two-Way Branching: The "if...else" Statement
content.definition: Guarantees that exactly ONE of two alternative blocks will execute: the 'if' block when True, or the 'else' block when False.
points: No condition on 'else': The 'else' keyword acts as the catch-all fallback.
Mutual Exclusivity: Both blocks can never execute together in the same run.

codeSnippet.code:
# Egyptian Driving License Eligibility Check
age = 17

if age >= 18:
    print('✅ Approved: Eligible to apply for driving license.')
else:
    years_left = 18 - age
    print('❌ Rejected: Underage applicant.')
    print(f'Please reapply in {years_left} year(s).')
codeSnippet.output:
❌ Rejected: Underage applicant.
Please reapply in 1 year(s).

content.title: Multi-Way Decisions: The "if...elif...else" Ladder
content.definition: Used when evaluating multiple mutual conditions sequentially from top to bottom.
points: First-Match Priority: As soon as a condition evaluates to True, its block runs and the rest are skipped.
Order Matters: Conditions must be ordered from strictest/highest to lowest.

content.title: Logical Operators: Combining Compound Conditions
content.definition: Logical operators (and, or, not) allow you to build sophisticated compound conditions.

table.desc: Returns True ONLY if BOTH conditions are True
Returns True if AT LEAST ONE condition is True
Inverts the Boolean value (True -> False, False -> True)

codeSnippet.code:
# Cairo STEM University Scholarship Eligibility
gpa = 3.8
extracurricular_score = 92
is_disciplinary_clean = True

if (gpa >= 3.7 and extracurricular_score >= 85) and not (is_disciplinary_clean == False):
    print('🎉 Congratulations! 100% Full Scholarship Awarded.')
else:
    print('Application placed on regular admission track.')
